tests.description: The muzzle, the flag point, aiming and firing of a tank made of nested custom objects follow every transformation (ToParentX/Y/Angle, FromParentX/Y/Angle), compared with what the renderer draws.
tests.name: TankConversions2D
source: // Gameplay test: a 2D tank (a custom object) containing a turret (a custom
// object) containing a cannon (a sprite with a "Muzzle" point). The scene
// only uses the interface of the tank: Tank.MuzzleX/Y/Angle(), FlagX/Y/Angle()
// (converted with ToParentX/Y/Angle at each level), AimAt and SetCannonHeading
// (converted with FromParentX/Y/Angle at each level). Everything is compared
// with where the renderer (Pixi) actually draws the parts of the tank.
const random = (min, max) => min + Math.random() * (max - min);
/** Where Pixi draws a pixel of the image of a sprite, in the scene. */
const angleOf = (from, to) => gdjs.toDegrees(Math.atan2(to.y - from.y, to.x - from.x));
/** What the game draws of a tank: its muzzle, its cannon, its flag point. */
/** Any transformation of the tank, and anything inside it. */
/** The tanks on a ring around the middle of the screen, for screenshots. */
/** Fire a few volleys, so the bullets draw where the cannons point. */
// 1. Whatever the transformations, the events give the muzzle, the cannon
// angle and the flag point that the game draws - and the flag attached by the
// events of the scene sits on it.
const worst = { muzzle: 0, muzzleAngle: 0, flagPoint: 0, flagAngle: 0, attachedFlag: 0, attachedFlagAngle: 0 };
worst.muzzle = Math.max(worst.muzzle, Math.hypot(state.MuzzleX - drawn.muzzle.x, state.MuzzleY - drawn.muzzle.y));
worst.flagPoint = Math.max(worst.flagPoint, Math.hypot(state.FlagX - drawn.flag.x, state.FlagY - drawn.flag.y));
worst.attachedFlag = Math.max(worst.attachedFlag, Math.hypot(flag.getX() - drawn.flag.x, flag.getY() - drawn.flag.y));
report('Muzzle and flag point, 200 random frames x 5 tanks', worst, 1e-3);
await harness.takeScreenshot('Random transformations - flags attached', { fullResolution: true });
// 2. Bullets fired by the scene from Tank.MuzzleX/Y, at Tank.MuzzleAngle(),
// leave the drawn muzzle along the drawn cannon.
const along = dx * Math.cos(direction) + dy * Math.sin(direction);
worst.distanceToCannonLine = Math.max(worst.distanceToCannonLine, Math.abs(-dx * Math.sin(direction) + dy * Math.cos(direction)));
// 400 pixels per second, for 20 or 21 frames.
harness.assert(isEveryBulletInFront, 'Every bullet flew forward from the muzzle, at its speed');
await harness.takeScreenshot('Bullets fired from Tank.MuzzleX-Y at Tank.MuzzleAngle', { fullResolution: true });
// 3. AimAt(MouseX(), MouseY()): the tank converts the cursor with FromParentX/Y,
// then the turret again: every drawn cannon points at the cursor.
const mouse = { x: mouseX, y: mouseY };
report('Aim at the cursor (FromParentX/Y)', { cannonToCursorAngle: worstAim }, 1e-3);
// The cursor in the middle, shown by a crosshair: every cannon points at it.
await harness.takeScreenshot('Aiming at the crosshair (FromParentX-Y) and firing', { fullResolution: true });
// And somewhere else, after the tanks moved.
await harness.takeScreenshot('Aiming at the crosshair after the tanks moved', { fullResolution: true });
// 4. SetCannonHeading(Heading): converted with FromParentAngle at each level,
// the drawn cannons face the heading given in the scene.
await harness.takeScreenshot('Every cannon facing up, heading -90 (FromParentAngle)', { fullResolution: true });
// 5. A collapsed tank (a scale of 0) still answers numbers, never NaN.
'A tank collapsed by a scale of 0 answers numbers: ' + JSON.stringify(state)
harness.assert(Number.isFinite(cannon.getAngle()), 'Aiming a collapsed tank never gives a NaN angle');

parameters: AngleBetweenPositions(Cannon.X(), Cannon.Y(), Object.FromParentX(TargetX, TargetY), Object.FromParentY(TargetX, TargetY))
